body:
## Why

An MCP server can send the model instructions of its own, as well as its tools. That exists for servers that anyone can plug into a client they don't control. We write every server and every agent, so we don't need it. Today the `trip` and `memory` servers send instructions (tool design, section 4). So the rules the coordinator follows would be split between its system prompt and two servers' instructions.

This issue moves those rules out of the servers. A rule that covers several tools goes in the system prompt of each agent that has those tools. Then everything the model is told, apart from each tool's own name, description, and input schema, is in one system prompt per agent. A system prompt is also per agent, and a server isn't. The `trip` server holds both the coordinator's tools and the workers' tools, so a rule written for the coordinator could reach a worker. It's done before #48, so #48 builds the coordinator without changing the tool servers.

## Design

- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), section 4.

## Open questions

- ~~Does the started-trip sentence in the `memory` server's instructions move to the coordinator's prompt? The sentence is "Once the trip has started, its trip memory can't change, and user memory still can." The `trip` server doesn't state its own started-trip rule, and the rule matters only in a turn still running at midnight, when the error already says the trip has started. "User memory still can" could also lead a coordinator whose trip memory add was refused to save the note to user memory instead, which would carry a one-trip note to every later trip.~~ Settled in chat on 2026-10-23: drop the sentence. The model learns the rule from the error, as with the `trip` server. Tool design section 4 and technical spec 3.1 still describe the rule. Raised by Joe on 2026-10-23, while reviewing PR #116.

## Do

- Change the "rule that covers several tools" bullet in tool design section 4. A rule that covers several tools goes in the system prompt of each agent that has those tools, not in an MCP server's instructions, and not in each tool's description. When the rule applies to more than one agent, its text is written once in code, and each agent's prompt that needs it includes it. A tool's description holds only what's specific to that tool, and the system prompt never repeats it. When an agent evaluation shows a model missing one of these rules, the rule is repeated in the description of the tool where it was missed. Drop the sentence about where Claude Code puts server instructions.
- Remove `instructions` from the `trip` server (`src/tools/trip-server.ts`) and the `memory` server (`src/tools/memory-server.ts`), along with the constants that hold the text, and fix any test or comment that refers to them. Fix the comment on `createWeatherServer` too, which says it needs no instructions because it has one tool.
- Don't put the removed text anywhere in this issue. #48's "Do" list holds it, word for word, and puts it in the coordinator's instructions. The started-trip sentence is dropped (open questions).

## Done when

- No MCP server in `src/` sets `instructions`.
- Tool design section 4 says where a rule that covers several tools goes, as above.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.
